Where we left them

Every NASA machine in our atlas, pinned at its real spot. Moon and Mars use NASA's own global maps, and each pin sits at the landing or crash coordinates. Drag a globe to spin it, tap a pin to open its mission card, or press play to watch them arrive year by year.

The maps

Moon: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio, CGI Moon Kit, colour map from the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera. Mars: NASA 3D Resources global Mars map. Both are real global mosaics; the globes are drawn from them pixel by pixel in your browser.

The pins

Landing and impact coordinates come from NASA mission records (NSSDCA) and published lists. Orbit rings around the globes are drawn for illustration. In deep space, the five escaping probes point in their real directions; other craft sit on their real orbit size, but their spot along the orbit is illustrative.

Live numbers

Distances of the escaping probes start from Wikipedia's table for 11 May 2026 and grow by each probe's speed, using today's date. Planet positions use average orbit speeds, so they can be a few degrees off.
